name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_UNIT8_Q01 - IUPAC classification of Group 12 and scandium

questiontext.text:
Read the following two statements and choose the correct option:

Statement I: Zinc, cadmium, and mercury have completely filled \((n-1)d^{10}\) configurations in their ground state as well as in their common oxidation states, and hence are not regarded as transition metals.

Statement II: Scandium (\(Z = 21\)) is regarded as a transition element because it has an incompletely filled \(3d^1\) orbital in its ground state.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
According to the IUPAC definition, transition metals are metals that possess an incompletely filled \(d\) subshell either in their neutral atom or in any of their common ions.

Step 2: Evaluation
The first claim is correct: Group 12 elements (\(\mathrm{Zn}\), \(\mathrm{Cd}\), and \(\mathrm{Hg}\)) possess \((n-1)d^{10}ns^2\) configurations in the ground state and \((n-1)d^{10}\) in their \(+2\) oxidation state, so they do not have an incomplete \(d\) subshell in either state and are not classified as transition metals. The second claim is also correct: scandium (\(Z = 21\)) has the ground-state configuration \([\mathrm{Ar}]3d^14s^2\), which contains an incompletely filled \(3d\) orbital, qualifying it as a transition element.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Both statements are factually correct.

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct, but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect, but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_UNIT8_Q02 - Periodic position and melting point peak in 3d series

questiontext.text:
Read the following two statements and choose the correct option:

Statement I: The \(d\)-block occupies the large middle section of the periodic table flanked between the \(s\)- and \(p\)-blocks, containing elements of Groups 3 to 12.

Statement II: In the \(3d\) transition series, manganese (\(Z = 25\)) has the highest melting point because it has five unpaired \(3d\) electrons.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The \(d\)-block consists of Groups 3–12 between the \(s\)- and \(p\)-blocks. Within a transition series, melting points rise to a maximum at the \(d^5\) configuration in Group 6 (\(\mathrm{Cr}\), \(\mathrm{Mo}\), \(\mathrm{W}\)), while Group 7 elements (\(\mathrm{Mn}\), \(\mathrm{Tc}\)) show anomalous dips.

Step 2: Evaluation
The first claim regarding the position of the \(d\)-block in the periodic table is correct. However, the second claim is incorrect: in the \(3d\) series, chromium (\(\mathrm{Cr}\), \(3d^54s^1\)) has the highest melting point, whereas manganese (\(\mathrm{Mn}\), \(3d^54s^2\)) exhibits an anomalously low melting point because its stable half-filled \(3d^5\) subshell reduces metallic bonding.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The first statement is correct, whereas the second statement is incorrect.

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct, but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect, but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_UNIT8_Q03 - Enthalpies of atomisation across transition series

questiontext.text:
Read the following two statements and choose the correct option:

Statement I: In the \(3d\) series from \(\mathrm{Sc}\) to \(\mathrm{Zn}\), copper has the lowest enthalpy of atomisation because of its completely filled \(3d^{10}\) subshell.

Statement II: Metals of the second (\(4d\)) and third (\(5d\)) transition series have greater enthalpies of atomisation than the corresponding elements of the first (\(3d\)) series, which accounts for more frequent metal–metal bonding in heavy transition metal compounds.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Enthalpy of atomisation measures the strength of interatomic metallic bonding, which depends on the number of valence electrons participating in bonding and the extent of orbital overlap.

Step 2: Evaluation
The first claim is incorrect: in the \(3d\) series, zinc (\(\mathrm{Zn}\))—not copper (\(\mathrm{Cu}\))—has the lowest enthalpy of atomisation (\(126\,\mathrm{kJ\,mol^{-1}}\) vs \(339\,\mathrm{kJ\,mol^{-1}}\) for \(\mathrm{Cu}\)), because no \(3d\) electrons are involved in metallic bonding in zinc. The second claim is correct: \(4d\) and \(5d\) metals have higher enthalpies of atomisation than \(3d\) metals, explaining the much more frequent occurrence of metal–metal bonding in compounds of heavy transition metals.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The first statement is incorrect, whereas the second statement is correct.

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct, but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect, but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_UNIT8_Q04 - Aqueous stability and electrode potential of copper

questiontext.text:
Read the following two statements and choose the correct option:

Statement I: In aqueous solution, \(\mathrm{Cu^+}\) is more stable than \(\mathrm{Cu^{2+}}\) because \(\mathrm{Cu^+}\) possesses a completely filled \(3d^{10}\) configuration.

Statement II: Metallic copper readily liberates hydrogen gas from dilute hydrochloric acid because its standard electrode potential \(E^\circ(\mathrm{Cu^{2+}/Cu})\) is negative.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Ion stability in aqueous solution depends on the balance between ionisation enthalpy and hydration enthalpy, while the ability of a metal to liberate \(\mathrm{H_2}\) from dilute acids requires a negative \(E^\circ(\mathrm{M^{2+}/M})\) value.

Step 2: Evaluation
The first claim is incorrect: \(\mathrm{Cu^{2+}}(aq)\) is much more stable than \(\mathrm{Cu^+}(aq)\) because the much more negative hydration enthalpy of \(\mathrm{Cu^{2+}}\) compensates for the second ionisation enthalpy of copper; \(\mathrm{Cu^+}(aq)\) undergoes disproportionation (\(2\mathrm{Cu^+} \rightarrow \mathrm{Cu^{2+}} + \mathrm{Cu}\)). The second claim is also incorrect: \(E^\circ(\mathrm{Cu^{2+}/Cu})\) is positive (\(+0.34\,\mathrm{V}\)), so copper cannot liberate \(\mathrm{H_2}\) from dilute non-oxidising acids like \(\mathrm{HCl}\).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Both statements are incorrect.

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct, but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect, but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_UNIT8_Q05 - Preparation and structure of potassium dichromate

questiontext.text:
Read the following two statements and choose the correct option:

Statement I: Potassium dichromate is prepared by treating a solution of sodium dichromate with potassium chloride because potassium dichromate is less soluble than sodium dichromate.

Statement II: In the dichromate ion (\(\mathrm{Cr_2O_7^{2-}}\)), chromium is in the \(+7\) oxidation state and the \(\mathrm{Cr\text{–}O\text{–}Cr}\) bond angle is \(180^\circ\).

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The preparation of \(\mathrm{K_2Cr_2O_7}\) from \(\mathrm{Na_2Cr_2O_7}\) relies on fractional crystallisation due to lower solubility, while the structure of \(\mathrm{Cr_2O_7^{2-}}\) consists of two corner-sharing \(\mathrm{CrO_4}\) tetrahedra.

Step 2: Evaluation
The first claim is correct: sodium dichromate is more soluble than potassium dichromate, so adding \(\mathrm{KCl}\) to \(\mathrm{Na_2Cr_2O_7}\) solution precipitates orange crystals of \(\mathrm{K_2Cr_2O_7}\). The second claim is incorrect: in \(\mathrm{Cr_2O_7^{2-}}\), chromium is in the \(+6\) oxidation state (same as in \(\mathrm{CrO_4^{2-}}\)), and the \(\mathrm{Cr\text{–}O\text{–}Cr}\) bond angle is \(126^\circ\), not \(180^\circ\).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The first statement is correct, whereas the second statement is incorrect.

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct, but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect, but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_UNIT8_Q06 - Structure and magnetic properties of manganate and permanganate

questiontext.text:
Read the following two statements and choose the correct option:

Statement I: Both the manganate (\(\mathrm{MnO_4^{2-}}\)) and permanganate (\(\mathrm{MnO_4^-}\)) ions are tetrahedral, with \(\pi\)-bonding taking place by overlap of \(p\) orbitals of oxygen with \(d\) orbitals of manganese.

Statement II: The green manganate ion is paramagnetic because of one unpaired electron, whereas the purple permanganate ion is diamagnetic due to the absence of unpaired electrons.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Manganate (\(\mathrm{MnO_4^{2-}}\)) and permanganate (\(\mathrm{MnO_4^-}\)) are oxoanions of manganese in the \(+6\) and \(+7\) oxidation states, respectively.

Step 2: Evaluation
The first claim is correct: both \(\mathrm{MnO_4^{2-}}\) and \(\mathrm{MnO_4^-}\) have tetrahedral geometry, and \(\pi\)-bonding arises from overlap of filled \(2p\) orbitals of oxygen with vacant \(3d\) orbitals of manganese. The second claim is also correct: \(\mathrm{MnO_4^{2-}}\) has \(\mathrm{Mn(VI)}\) with a \(3d^1\) configuration (one unpaired electron, paramagnetic), whereas \(\mathrm{MnO_4^-}\) has \(\mathrm{Mn(VII)}\) with a \(3d^0\) configuration (zero unpaired electrons, diamagnetic).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Both statements are factually correct.

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct, but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect, but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_UNIT8_Q07 - Oxidation states and redox behaviour of lanthanoids

questiontext.text:
Read the following two statements and choose the correct option:

Statement I: In the lanthanoid series, \(\mathrm{Eu^{2+}}\) (\(4f^7\)) and \(\mathrm{Yb^{2+}}\) (\(4f^{14}\)) act as strong oxidising agents, whereas \(\mathrm{Ce^{4+}}\) (\(4f^0\)) acts as a strong reducing agent.

Statement II: The \(+3\) oxidation state is the most stable oxidation state for all lanthanoids, and all tripositive lanthanoid ions (\(\mathrm{Ln^{3+}}\)) have the general electronic configuration \([\mathrm{Xe}]4f^n\) (\(n = 1\) to \(14\)).

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
For all lanthanoids, \(+3\) is the predominant and most stable oxidation state. Ions in \(+2\) or \(+4\) states form when stabilised by \(f^0\), \(f^7\), or \(f^{14}\) configurations, but they readily revert to the \(+3\) state.

Step 2: Evaluation
The first claim is incorrect: \(\mathrm{Eu^{2+}}\) and \(\mathrm{Yb^{2+}}\) tend to lose an electron to reach the common \(+3\) state, so they are strong reducing agents (reductants), whereas \(\mathrm{Ce^{4+}}\) tends to gain an electron to reach \(\mathrm{Ce^{3+}}\), making it a strong oxidant (\(E^\circ = +1.74\,\mathrm{V}\)). The second claim is correct: \(+3\) is the most stable oxidation state of all lanthanoids, and \(\mathrm{Ln^{3+}}\) ions have the \([\mathrm{Xe}]4f^n\) configuration.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The first statement is incorrect, whereas the second statement is correct.

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct, but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect, but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_UNIT8_Q08 - Actinoid contraction and oxidation state range

questiontext.text:
Read the following two statements and choose the correct option:

Statement I: Actinoid contraction is smaller from element to element than lanthanoid contraction because \(5f\) electrons shield the nuclear charge more effectively than \(4f\) electrons.

Statement II: Actinoids exhibit a narrower range of oxidation states than lanthanoids because the \(5f\), \(6d\), and \(7s\) levels in actinoids have widely separated energies.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Actinoid properties are governed by poor shielding by \(5f\) electrons and the comparable energies of the \(5f\), \(6d\), and \(7s\) orbitals.

Step 2: Evaluation
The first claim is incorrect: actinoid contraction is greater from element to element than lanthanoid contraction because \(5f\) electrons provide poorer shielding from the nuclear charge than \(4f\) electrons. The second claim is also incorrect: actinoids exhibit a much wider range of oxidation states (up to \(+7\) in \(\mathrm{Np}\) and \(\mathrm{Pu}\)) than lanthanoids precisely because the \(5f\), \(6d\), and \(7s\) energy levels are of comparable energies.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Both statements are incorrect.

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct, but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect, but Statement II is correct.
